To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a factored, random field source model can learn to disambiguation morphological analysis in context, and (ii) this source model can be used in conjunction with a channel model to achieve statistically significant error rate reduction over baseline state-of-the- art methods on Korean, Arabic and Czech.

(1) the proposed method achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art disambiguation methods on three languages with very different morphology, (2) the proposed method is able to learn to disambiguated from a small training set, and (3) the proposed method performs better on the full task than on individual subtasks.

1) a factored random field is an effective model for morphological disambigu-ation in context; 2) this method is robust with respect to the size of training data and is effective on languages with different morphologies; 3) this method can be applied to a variety of morphological tasks; and 4) this method is applicable to both concatenative and templatic languages.
